# Two bounds of a product of two bounds of intervals, two limbs

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `mul_ext_2_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Two bounds of $x y$, of two limbs, within $A\lvert x y\rvert + B$ of it:

$$l \le x y \le h.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $y = y_0 + y_1$, $l = l_0 + l_1$, $h = h_0 + h_1$.

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`interval_mul_2`](interval_mul_2.md).

## Requires

- $x$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.
- $x$ is not a NaN: a finite normalized pair or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$.
- $y$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.
- $y$ is not a NaN: a finite normalized pair or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $l$, $h$ are canonical.
- When every operand and $l$ and $h$ are finite, the statement on finite operands holds:
    - $l$ is normalized: $l_0 = \mathrm{RN}(l_0 + l_1)$.
    - $h$ is normalized: $h_0 = \mathrm{RN}(h_0 + h_1)$.
- If an operand is a zero: $l$ is a zero, whatever the other operand, $\pm\infty$ included ($0 \cdot \infty = 0$, the product of two bounds in interval arithmetic).
- $l$ is never a NaN.
- If an operand is infinite and none is a zero: $l = x y$ as `T` computes it on the leading limbs, the infinity of the sign of the product.
- If every operand is finite: $l \le x y$ (an infinite $l$ is $-\infty$), and when $l$ is finite, $\lvert l - (x y)\rvert \le A\,\lvert x y\rvert + B$, with the constants $A$ and $B$ below.
- If an operand is a zero: $h$ is a zero, whatever the other operand, $\pm\infty$ included ($0 \cdot \infty = 0$, the product of two bounds in interval arithmetic).
- $h$ is never a NaN.
- If an operand is infinite and none is a zero: $h = x y$ as `T` computes it on the leading limbs, the infinity of the sign of the product.
- If every operand is finite: $h \ge x y$ (an infinite $h$ is $+\infty$), and when $h$ is finite, $\lvert h - (x y)\rvert \le A\,\lvert x y\rvert + B$, with the constants $A$ and $B$ below.

The constants of the bound, from `gen/claims.json`: $A$ is `(2*(1+u)^3*up((1+u)^6)*up(unit(mul_2_2)/(1-unit(mul_2_2)))+2*u^2)*(1+unit(mul_2_2))/(1-u)` and $B$ is `2*(1+u)^2*(1/2*up((1+u)^6)*eta+up((1+u)*(2*(1+u)^5*eta+tiny(mul_2_2)/(1-unit(mul_2_2))+eta/2)+eta/(2*u)))+eta+(2*(1+u)^3*up((1+u)^6)*up(unit(mul_2_2)/(1-unit(mul_2_2)))+2*u^2)/(1-u)*tiny(mul_2_2)`, where `up( )` is a constant as `T` rounds it up (the $E$, $G$, $H$ of a radius) and `unit( )`, `tiny( )` are the constants of the center's kernel; $N$ is the smallest normal number of `T`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| $A / u^2$ | $1.0000000000000013 \times 10^{1}$ | $1.0000006794931444 \times 10^{1}$ |
| $B / N$ | $2.0000000000000031 \times 10^{0}$ | $2.000001668930274 \times 10^{0}$ |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 4 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `mul_ext_2_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalMul2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalMul2.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions mul_ext_2_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `mul_ext_2_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** mul_dir_2_2, with the products of a zero and of an infinity selected (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/mul_ext_2_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/mul_ext_2_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`mul_dir_2_2`](mul_dir_2_2.md).

```
# The product of two bounds of intervals with 2-limb bounds, enclosed between two canonical 2-limb
# values l and h (milestone2.md, "Interval kernels", "Two limbs"). The operands are canonical and
# not NaN. A zero operand gives zero whatever the other one (0 times infinity is 0, the product of
# two bounds in interval arithmetic); otherwise an infinite operand gives the infinite product, as
# both values; otherwise mul_dir_2_2, and a value of it that is not finite becomes the infinity on
# its side (-inf for l, +inf for h), which is always a bound. For finite operands and a finite
# value the claims of mul_dir_2_2 hold of it, with its constants: on its side of x y, within
# A |x y| + B, normalized.

(c0, c1, e0, e1) = mul_dir_2_2(x0, x1, y0, y1)
t   = prod(x0, y0)
ax  = abs(x0)
fx  = lt(ax, const inf)
ay  = abs(y0)
fy  = lt(ay, const inf)
fo  = and(fx, fy)
zx  = eq(x0, 0)
zy  = eq(y0, 0)
zz  = or(zx, zy)
nz  = not(zz)
ac  = abs(c0)
fc  = lt(ac, const inf)
ae  = abs(e0)
fe  = lt(ae, const inf)
mi  = neg(const inf)
p0  = select(fc, c0, mi)
p1  = select(fc, c1, 0)
q0  = select(fe, e0, const inf)
q1  = select(fe, e1, 0)
r0  = select(fo, p0, t)
r1  = select(fo, p1, 0)
s0  = select(fo, q0, t)
s1  = select(fo, q1, 0)
l0  = select(nz, r0, 0)
l1  = select(nz, r1, 0)
h0  = select(nz, s0, 0)
h1  = select(nz, s1, 0)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#mul_ext_2_2)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 12 998 613 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- Which canonical value comes out when an operand is not finite: the claims say only that it is canonical.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
